media_item.focus_or_theme: Exoneration after decades based on recanted witness testimony.
media_item.summary_notes: Profiles the case of three men spending a combined 100+ years in prison based on false testimony from a 12-year-old who later recanted. Focuses on the exonerations of Ricky Jackson, Wiley Bridgeman, and Kwame Ajamu in Cleveland after Eddie Vernon recanted his testimony.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Profiles case of three men spending combined 100+ years based on false testimony of 12-year-old boy who later recanted. Available via ABC/Hulu.
research_notes_other.research_findings: While searches didn't confirm a specific Nightline episode with this title, the details match the high-profile exoneration of Ricky Jackson, Wiley Bridgeman, and Kwame Ajamu in Cleveland. Their convictions rested almost entirely on the testimony of a young boy, Eddie Vernon, who recanted decades later, stating police coerced him. Jackson's 39 years served was the longest known US wrongful imprisonment at the time of his release. Case details above rely on list info and public knowledge consistent with the list description.

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Wrongfully convicted of murder in 1975 and sentenced to death (later commuted to life). Served nearly 39 years before being exonerated in 2014. His conviction was based on false witness testimony from a 12-year-old who later recanted.
contributing_factors_raw: False witness testimony (by 12-year-old Eddie Vernon, who recanted years later)
